title: Terminal Velocity
desc: Extreme altitudes, sinking cities & the places where maps give up

questions.q: Jakarta is sinking so fast the Indonesian government is building a new capital. How fast is it sinking?
questions.a: Up to 25cm per year in parts — largely due to groundwater extraction. The new capital is called Nusantara, on Borneo
A narrow strip of territory extending from a wider area — like the Oklahoma or Florida panhandles, or the Wakhan Corridor in Afghanistan

questions.q: The Bermuda Triangle is famous — but which body of water has more documented shipwrecks per square mile?
questions.a: The Great Lakes — particularly Lake Superior, which has claimed over 350 ships

questions.q: What is the Caspian Sea — technically?
questions.a: The world's largest enclosed inland body of water. Legally it's classified as neither a lake nor a sea — a 2018 convention gave it 'special legal status'

questions.q: Doggerland connected Britain to mainland Europe until roughly when?
questions.a: About 6,500 BC — rising sea levels after the last ice age submerged it. Fishermen still trawl up mammoth bones and stone tools

questions.q: What makes the Sargasso Sea unique among all the world's seas?
questions.a: It has no coastline — it's defined entirely by ocean currents (the North Atlantic gyre). It's the only sea bounded by water, not land

questions.q: Svalbard, Norway has a 'doomsday vault'. What's stored in it?
questions.a: Seeds — the Svalbard Global Seed Vault holds over 1 million seed samples from nearly every country, as insurance against global crop failure

questions.q: What is a 'desire path' in urban geography?
questions.a: A footpath created by foot traffic where people actually walk, as opposed to where planners put pavements — a physical record of collective human preference

questions.q: The antipodal point of London (exact opposite side of Earth) is where?
questions.a: In the ocean southeast of New Zealand — most of Europe's antipodes are in the Pacific Ocean
